item.title: Connection of surface code patches based on entanglement distillation without postselection
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Moeto Mishima, Toshihiko Sasaki, Yasunari Suzuki, Koji Azuma, Masato Koashi
arXiv:2611.06260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distributed quantum computing is a promising approach for overcoming the scalability limitations of fault-tolerant quantum computing. Entanglement distillation, a process that extracts higher-fidelity entangled states from noisy ones, plays a key role in distributed quantum computing. However, simple distillation protocols typically rely on postselection, which poses practical challenges for implementation. Here, we propose a scheme for distributed surface-code quantum computing that benefits from entanglement distillation even without postselection. 👤 Rajat Pandey, Alok Kumar Pan
arXiv:2611.06337v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The entangled basis measurement plays a pivotal role in fundamental information-processing tasks, such as dense coding, quantum teleportation, and entanglement swapping. Consequently, certifying such measurements in a device-independent manner remains an important task. In this work, we present a semi-device-independent (SDI) protocol in a prepare-and-measure (PM) scenario for certifying a class of m-qubit entangled basis measurements. Specifically, we consider a tripartite PM scenario featuring two senders and one receiver, where each sender sends an arbitrary number of 2^m inputs and the receiver performs a measurement with 2^m outcomes. 👤 Qi Han, Shijiao Xing, Xuexin Huang, Xiao Wu and Junlin Li
In this paper, we investigate entanglement routing in hexagonal lattice hypergraph quantum networks (HLHQNs) under 2-localization and hypergraph immersion. Firstly, we model each hexagonal face as a six-partite GHZ hyperedge, and show that each hexagonal GHZ hyperedge admits deterministic 2-localization, namely, it can be converted via local operations and classical communication into a Bell state between any designated pair of vertices. This property is further generalized to arbitrary -partite GHZ states. arXiv:2507.06770v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum relays are central to both quantum communication and distributed quantum computing, enabling long-distance transmission and modular architectures. Our three-terminal relay model captures the trade-off between repeater-assisted and repeaterless communication strategies. arXiv:2611.05757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pure states of four and seven qubits cannot be maximally entangled across every balanced bipartition; we determine how entangled they can be on average. For four qubits we prove the conjecture of Higuchi and Sudbery: the mean von Neumann entropy of the three 2|2 cuts is at most 1+tfrac12łog₂ 3 bits, with equality exactly on the local-unitary orbits of their state M₄ and its complex conjugate. For seven qubits the mean purity of the 35 balanced 3|4 cuts is at least 121/917 and their mean entropy is at most 2.965356029łdots bits, each with a unique optimiser up to local unitaries and qubit permutations. arXiv:2611.05497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Entanglement swapping entangles photons that never interacted directly. item.title: Hybrid Clifford Codes via Operator Algebra Quantum Error Correction and Projective Representation Theory
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Jonas Eidesen, David W. Kribs, Andrew Nemec
arXiv:2606.02531v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Clifford codes are a natural generalization of quantum stabilizer codes based primarily on representation theory. This class of codes has previously been extended to the setting of quantum subsystem codes. We formulate a two-fold generalization of Clifford codes, for both the hybrid classical and quantum information and projective representation theory settings. This leads to new classes of hybrid subspace and subsystem Clifford codes. We extend the fundamental representation theoretic quantum error correction theorem to include these codes, based on the operator algebra quantum error correction framework. We also discuss several examples throughout the presentation, of both stabilizer and non-stabilizer type.

item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Yi Liang
arXiv:2611.06215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vanishing-error recovery of a fusion qubit from a fixed-sector ground doublet of four Kramers--Wannier defects in a critical Ising chain requires at least the shorter three-defect span of physical spins to leading order. Across arbitrary preselected spin sets and unrestricted joint decoding, this bound holds when the thermodynamic limit precedes large spacings at fixed positive ratios. An exact interval decoder attains it. Collective records of both logical axes in the complement force successful near-minimal supports to concentrate in density on a leading-order shortest interval.
